# DIS (Walt Disney Company) — Value Investor Note

## Circle of Competence
Understandable at the business-model level: content and IP creation, distribution (linear + streaming), and physical experiences (theme parks, cruises, consumer products). No exotic financial engineering. The live judgment call is how fast linear-TV economics fade versus how fast streaming/DTC economics scale to replace them - a real strategic question, not a settled one.

## Moat & Durability — Score 6/10
Disney Experiences is a near-unassailable moat: multi-decade capital intensity, scarce real estate, and a self-reinforcing IP flywheel (Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar, the Disney animation vault) that competitors cannot replicate at any price. That segment alone would score 8-9. But Disney is one company, and linear networks (ABC, ESPN, Disney Channel) are in genuine structural decline from cord-cutting, while Disney+/Hulu streaming - now profitable - competes in a market with low consumer switching costs and real price competition from Netflix, Amazon, and Apple. Blended across the whole entity, the moat is real but under active erosion at the media-networks edge, hence 6, not 8.

## Management & Capital Allocation
ROE of 8.0% looks unimpressive for a franchise business, but this is mostly an artifact of the large equity base left over from the 2019 Fox acquisition, not necessarily poor incremental returns on new capital. Debt/equity near 39% is moderate and consistent with continued deleveraging since the Fox deal. Under Iger's return, the company refocused on cost discipline and streaming profitability; the market's forward P/E of 14.4x against a trailing 21.6x implies real credibility for an earnings inflection. What this packet cannot verify: actual buyback pace, dividend payout, succession planning beyond Iger's tenure, or insider ownership alignment. Treat 'trustworthy management' as a reasonable but unverified inference.

## Predictability
Earnings are more predictable than during the pandemic-and-streaming-loss years, but this still fails Munger's 'easy decision' bar. The forward P/E already prices in roughly a 50% one-year jump in net income that depends on streaming-margin execution still underway, and ESPN's pivot to direct-to-consumer is an unproven model transition for the company's historically most profitable segment. Revenue growth of 6.8% is respectable but not the low-variance compounding Munger rewards with a quality premium, and Experiences results carry real macro sensitivity (beta 1.4).

## Inversion — How an Owner Loses Money From Here
1. **Forward-earnings shortfall**: streaming and ESPN DTC margins fail to reach what the 14.4x forward P/E already assumes, and the multiple re-rates back toward the trailing 21.6x, compressing the stock even if the business is merely 'fine.'
2. **Linear decline outruns DTC**: cord-cutting erodes ABC/ESPN/cable-network profits faster than streaming and parks can offset, structurally shrinking a historically high-margin cash-flow segment.
3. **Capex cycle meets a soft consumer**: a discretionary-spending pullback (beta 1.4) hits Experiences bookings just as the segment is mid-cycle on heavy new capex (parks expansion, cruise ships), squeezing the already-thin 2.6% FCF yield further.

## Valuation
The packet gives market cap ($184.5B), trailing P/E (21.6x), forward P/E (14.4x), and FCF yield (2.6%) but not share count or price directly. Back-solving: trailing net income ≈ market cap / P/E ≈ $8.5B; forward (consensus) net income ≈ market cap / forward P/E ≈ $12.8B - implying the market expects roughly a 50% jump in earnings power. Assuming a diluted share count near 1.8B (a modeling assumption, not sourced from the packet, but consistent with Disney's known scale) implies a current price near $103/share, trailing EPS near $4.75, and FCF/share near $2.70 - a wide EPS-to-FCF gap driven by the elevated Experiences capex cycle (this checks out internally: price/EPS ≈ 21.6x and price/forward-EPS ≈ 14.4x, matching the packet's stated multiples).

Normalizing owner earnings conservatively toward ~$5.50/share (above trailing EPS to give partial credit for the streaming margin ramp already underway, but well short of the $7.13 forward-consensus figure since a 50% one-year net-income jump is optimistic until proven in results), and applying a Munger-conservative 15x-18x multiple (below top-tier moat multiples because of the linear-TV drag on the blended business), gives a fair value range of roughly **$82-$99/share**, midpoint ~$90.50. Against an implied current price of ~$103, that is a margin of safety of roughly **-11.7%** - the stock is priced slightly ahead of a conservative estimate of intrinsic value, not sitting at a discount.

## The Cloning Caveat
Eighteen superinvestor buy/add rows span Q1-Q2 2026, but position sizes are broadly small: the largest is Viking Global's add landing at 0.57% of portfolio, and most of the rest - Tweedy Browne's new 0.33% stake, Pzena's eye-catching 879% share increase that nonetheless lands at just 0.22% of portfolio, Ariel's 0.10%, Semper Augustus's two adds totaling under 0.2% combined, Gardner Russo & Quinn's (Tom Russo, a well-known patient quality/moat investor) add at effectively 0.0% - are basket-level exposure, not statement positions. The breadth across several genuine value and quality-focused shops is real corroboration that Disney is not obviously overvalued or a value trap, but none of them is betting big on it here. This supports 'reasonable, not dangerous' - it is not evidence of a mispriced bargain, and it does not override the valuation math above.

## Verdict
**Watch, conviction 4/10.** A real, if partially eroding, moat (best-in-class parks/IP offset by declining linear TV) attached to a management team that has stabilized streaming economics but whose forward numbers still need to be proven out. At an implied ~$103/share against a conservative fair-value midpoint of ~$90.50, there is no margin of safety today - the market has already priced in the earnings inflection the forward P/E implies. Revisit if the price falls into the low-$80s-to-$90s range, or if realized (not forward-estimated) earnings confirm the streaming/ESPN DTC margin ramp - either would meaningfully improve the risk/reward without requiring a change in the underlying business thesis.
momentum_thesis: DIS is a sharp one-month reversal (+7.9%) sitting on top of a stock that's still down 6.5% over 12 months and only 1.3% above its 200DMA — the tape has flipped but the trend hasn't been re-established yet, and RSI14 at 75.5 says the bounce has already run hot into overbought territory with limited fuel left before a pullback. There's no short base to squeeze (1.13% of float, 1.78 days to cover), so this isn't a positioning-driven melt-up; the modestly bullish put/call skew (0.67) reflects genuine directional conviction rather than crowded shorts capitulating. What stands out is the superinvestor tape: over a dozen value managers piled in across both Q1 and Q2 2026 — Duan Yongping/H&H doubled down twice (+112%, then +12.9%), Pzena added 879%, and Tweedy Browne and First Pacific initiated new positions — buying into a name still red on the year, which is a classic value-crowd-buys-weakness signal rather than a momentum chase. That accumulation gives the recent pop a fundamental floor and lowers the odds of a full round-trip back to the lows, but it doesn't change the fact that the technical setup (overbought RSI, barely-positive 200DMA, still-negative 6/12m trend) is fragile and unconfirmed. Net: constructive but not clean — the smart-money accumulation argues for buying dips rather than chasing the current overbought print.
